records.rationale: The limits-to-asymptotes connection is correct, but the vertical-asymptote statement uses an unqualified two-sided limit. A single divergent one-sided limit is enough, and the opposite side may diverge differently or stay finite.

evidence.title: University of Toronto, One-sided Limits
evidence.finding: A vertical asymptote is established when either one-sided limit is positive or negative infinity; a common two-sided infinite limit is not required.
Let f(x)=1/x for x>0 and f(x)=0 for x<0. The right-side limit at 0 is +infinity, giving a vertical asymptote, while the left limit is 0; no common two-sided infinite limit exists.
Horizontal asymptotes can likewise refer to either end separately; the hold principally concerns the stated vertical-limit notation.

evidence.finding: The top exterior power of an n-dimensional vector space is one-dimensional. The induced map Lambda^n(T) is scalar multiplication by det(T); expanding a basis wedge gives the determinant's alternating sum.

records.rationale: The labels describe two possible enforcement patterns, but the claimed drift disadvantage of post-step projection is misleading. Projection or correction can itself remove constraint drift; its effectiveness depends on the constraint, tolerances and projection method.

evidence.title: SciML, Manifold Projection
evidence.finding: Post-step projection corrects the solution onto a specified manifold to preserve a constraint or conserved property; it is itself a mechanism for controlling drift.

For the linear constraint x=0, projecting each tentative step (x_tilde,y_tilde) to (0,y_tilde) makes the constraint residual exactly zero at every corrected endpoint without an additional Baumgarte term.
This does not assert exact conservation of all properties by an arbitrary numerical projection or conflate endpoint projection with internal-stage constraints.
